newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rate down to 11.9 pct from 13.4.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rate down to 11.9 pct from 13.4.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slumped to 11.9 pct on Monday from 13.4 in slow trade marked by weak demand for kuna funds at Zagreb's money market.
Daily settlements totalled a modest 19.8 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 15.2 on the supply side.
Fresh loans accounted for 15 million kuna.
Call money deals, accounting for most of the fresh and rolled over borrowings, were struck at a steady 10.5 percent.
New interbank loans were made at 13 and 16 percent.
A private issuer also sold for the first time two million kuna in six-month commercial notes at eight percent a year.
The Zagreb Stock Exchange rolled over a one-month borrowing at 15 percent, while banks charged 14, 16 and 17 percent respectively for two-week, one-month and three-month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Tuesday weaker at 6.0708 against the dollar and 3.5761 against the German mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
